outcome: Since 26 January 2024 I found no settlement, counterexample or AI-produced result on the threefold statement; the only dated activity is a 23 September 2024 arXiv revision of Mori and Prokhorov's 2020 partial result (reducible central curve, under an index hypothesis) that concedes an earlier statement was false in two subcases, plus a 2025 Sbornik remark by the same authors whose content I could not read.
problem_asks: Statement (Wikipedia, frozen January 2024): 'General elephant problem: do general elephants have at most Du Val singularities?' Parts, from the statement alone. (1) Object: a general member D of the anticanonical linear system |−K_X| of a variety X, which the article calls a general elephant (an idiosyncratic name introduced by Miles Reid). (2) Dimension: the question is for threefolds (the article: 'For 3-folds ... asks whether general elephants have at most du Val singularities'). (3) Quantifier: the bullet places no restriction on X. It names no Fano, Gorenstein, terminal, Mori-contraction or local-germ hypothesis, so as written it asks about every threefold for which the general elephant is defined. (4) Conclusion: a general elephant has at most Du Val (ADE) singularities, meaning every singular point is of ADE type; smooth counts as 'at most'. The bullet does not separately ask for normality. (5) 'General' is part of the claim: a single non-Du Val member of |−K_X| is not by itself a counterexample. Note for the later pass: the literature usually states Reid's conjecture for threefold Mori contractions over a neighbourhood (a local statement), and Q-Fano threefolds appear as a separate setting. The bullet's wording does not choose between these, so the record reports results under both readings.

events.what_happened: M. Reid's survey 'Young person's guide to canonical singularities' (Algebraic Geometry, Bowdoin 1985, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 46, AMS, 1987) introduces the name 'elephant' and formulates the general elephant conjecture; the Wikipedia article cites it. Prokhorov's 2021 survey (arXiv 2108.13052, Prop. 3.2) attributes to Reid a local version: for a terminal threefold singularity of index greater than 1, the general member of |−K_X| is Du Val. I did not open Reid's survey; both points come from the 2021 survey text and the Wikipedia article. AI check: not applicable to a 1987 source; nothing in the sources I read names a system.
events.delivers: Introduces the conjecture for threefold contractions: a general member of |−K_X| is a normal surface with Du Val singularities. The only result attributed to this source is the local statement at terminal points of index greater than 1 (survey Prop. 3.2). Nothing global, and no Fano case.
events.remains: The global statement for threefolds in the bullet's generality. This event introduces the conjecture rather than settling any part of it.
events.time_since_posted: about 39 years before 2026 (1987); not assessed as a recent result
events.direction: Formulates the conjecture; the local terminal-point statement goes the way the conjecture predicts.

events.what_happened: Shokurov and Reid, as credited in secondary sources I read: a Fano threefold with only canonical Gorenstein singularities has an anticanonical member whose only singularities are Du Val. Reid's 1980 'Canonical 3-folds' is the usual reference, but I only recalled that year from memory and found no source giving it, so no date is recorded. Attested in Prokhorov's 2021 survey (arXiv 2108.13052), a Tokyo seminar abstract (opened only as a search snippet), and a Kawakita survey (snippet only). I did not find the original text. AI check: nothing in the sources I read names a system.
events.delivers: For canonical Gorenstein Fano threefolds: existence of an anticanonical member with only Du Val singularities. The sources disagree on whether the member is 'an elephant' (Tokyo seminar abstract) or the general member (a Kawakita survey snippet calls the irreducible surface S with Du Val singularities the general elephant). Not resolved here.
events.remains: Non-Gorenstein Fano threefolds (where the answer is negative in some cases, event 13), and every non-Fano threefold setting. Whether the member is general, under the stricter reading, is unresolved.
events.doubts: Only secondary citations read. The wording ('an elephant' versus 'general') differs across the sources I saw, and I could not check the original.
events.direction: Confirms the Du Val conclusion, for canonical Gorenstein Fano threefolds only.

events.what_happened: Kollár and Mori, 'Classification of three-dimensional flips', J. Amer. Math. Soc. 5 (1992) 533–703 (DOI 10.1090/S0894-0347-1992-1149195-9). Their Theorem 2.2, as cited in Mori–Prokhorov 2020 (Thm 1.1), proves the conjecture for extremal curve germs with irreducible central curve: a general member of |−K_X| is a normal surface with Du Val singularities. I read this only as cited in arXiv 2002.10693 and in Chen 2016 (withdrawn, event 14); I did not open KM92. AI check: nothing read names a system.
events.revisions: Mori, erratum to the classification, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 20 (2007) 269–271 (AMS errata record S0894-0347-06-00543-1), making two corrections. I could not open it (403), so I do not know whether either correction touches Theorem 2.2.
events.delivers: For extremal curve germs (a terminal threefold germ with a contraction) whose central curve is irreducible, a general member of |−K_X| is a normal surface with only Du Val singularities.
events.remains: Extremal germs whose central curve is reducible. Mori and Prokhorov address part of that under an index hypothesis (event 16).
events.doubts: Mori's 2007 erratum corrects KM92 in two places; whether either affects the statement used here is not established from what I read. Chen's 2016 withdrawal (event 14) relies on this theorem for the flip case, which suggests the theorem is widely used.
events.direction: Confirms the Du Val conclusion for the irreducible-central-curve case.

events.what_happened: Mori and Prokhorov, 'On Q-conic bundles', arXiv math/0603736 (v1 31 Mar 2006; v2 6 Aug 2007), Publ. RIMS 44 (2008) 315–369 (cited as [MP08] in arXiv 2002.10693). The abstract (opened) says a corollary is that the base surface of every Q-conic bundle has only Du Val singularities of type A, which the authors call a positive solution of a conjecture of Iskovskikh; the paper also classifies Q-conic bundles when the singular fibre is irreducible and the base is singular. A search snippet of the table of contents lists a section on 'general (bi)elephants' for two non-Gorenstein points; I did not read that section. AI check: abstract and arXiv page only; nothing in them names a system.
events.delivers: Not established from what I read. The abstract concerns the Du Val type of the base surface. Whether the general (bi)elephant section proves a Du Val general member is unknown to me.
events.remains: The general-elephant question for Q-conic bundles over a singular base is treated in the later Part II (event 5); this event does not settle it as far as I can tell.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2008 (referee process not inspected)

events.direction: Not determinable from the abstract; I read no direct statement about general members.

events.what_happened: Mori and Prokhorov, 'On Q-conic bundles, II', arXiv 0710.0792 (v1 3 Oct 2007), Publ. RIMS 44 (2008) 955–971. The abstract (opened) says they obtain a complete classification of Q-conic bundle germs when the base surface germ is singular, generalising their earlier paper, which assumed the central fibre irreducible. ArXiv 2002.10693 (Thm 1.2) cites [MP08b] for Reid's conjecture for an arbitrary central curve in the Q-conic over singular base case. I infer that MP08b is this paper; the abstract does not mention elephants, and I did not read the body. AI check: abstract only; nothing names a system.
events.delivers: Per the 2020 paper's Theorem 1.2, as cited and not read here: a general member of |−K_X| is a normal surface with Du Val singularities for Q-conic bundle germs over a singular base, with arbitrary (possibly reducible) central curve. The abstract by itself does not state this.
events.remains: Q-conic bundles over a smooth base. Those remain conditional (Prokhorov 1996, event 10).

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2008 (referee process not inspected)

events.doubts: The attribution of Theorem 1.2's proof to this paper is my inference from the citation in 2002.10693, not checked against the body.
events.direction: Per the 2020 paper's citation: confirms the Du Val conclusion for Q-conic bundles over a singular base.

events.what_happened: Mori and Prokhorov, 'On Q-conic bundles, III', arXiv 0809.0489 (v1 2 Sep 2008), Publ. RIMS 45 (2009) 787–810. The abstract (opened) says the authors prove 'the existence of a Du Val anti-canonical member under the assumption that the central fiber is irreducible', for Q-conic bundle germs (a threefold with terminal singularities, a normal surface base, connected fibres, relatively ample −K). ArXiv 2002.10693 cites MP09 for the irreducible-central-curve Q-conic case of the conjecture (its Thm 1.1). AI check: abstract only; nothing names a system.
events.revisions: Single arXiv version; journal Publ. RIMS 45 (2009).
events.delivers: Existence of a Du Val member of |−K_X| for Q-conic bundle germs with irreducible central fibre. The abstract says 'existence', not 'general member'; the 2020 paper reads it as the general-member statement for that case.
events.remains: Q-conic bundle germs with reducible central fibre (covered in part by events 5 and 16). The existence-versus-general distinction for the irreducible case also remains open on the abstract's wording.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2009 (referee process not inspected)

events.doubts: The abstract says 'existence of a Du Val anti-canonical member'; Reid's conjecture is about the general member. I did not read the body to see whether the general member is proved. The 2020 paper treats the result as covering the general member.
events.direction: Confirms the Du Val conclusion, in existence form, for Q-conic bundles with irreducible central fibre.

events.what_happened: Kawakita, 'General elements in anticanonical systems of threefolds with divisorial contractions and applications to classification', arXiv math/0110050 (v1 4 Oct 2001; 41 pages; a single version). Theorem 1.1 (read in the ar5iv rendering): for a divisorial contraction whose exceptional divisor E contracts to a cDV point P, a general element of |−K_Y| has at worst Du Val singularities. The introduction says Shokurov, Reid and Takagi 'sustain it by affirmative answers for Fano threefolds with singularities'. A 'strong version' (the Du Val type at each point matches that of a general Du Val section) is attributed to this paper in a search digest; I did not verify it in the body. AI check: nothing read names a system.
events.delivers: For divisorial contractions Y→X whose exceptional divisor contracts to a cDV point, a general member of |−K_Y| has at worst Du Val singularities (Thm 1.1). Confined to that contraction type.
events.remains: Other contraction types (flips, conic bundles, extremal contractions to non-cDV points) and the Fano case beyond the cited introduction. The strong version is unverified.

checked_by.qualification: Researcher on the three-fold MMP who has written on this conjecture himself
checked_by.what_they_did: Restates a Kawakita divisorial-contraction theorem as a known result (Thm 4.1 in the survey); no independent check of the proof is reported

events.doubts: No specific error found, and I did not check the proof. The later JAMS paper (event 8) is by the same author, so it is not an independent confirmation.
events.direction: Confirms the Du Val conclusion for the cDV-point divisorial case.

events.what_happened: Kawakita, 'General elephants of three-fold divisorial contractions', J. Amer. Math. Soc. 16 (2003) 331–362 (DOI 10.1090/S0894-0347-02-00416-2). The JAMS page returned 403 to my fetch. A search snippet of it says the paper treats divisorial contractions whose exceptional divisor shrinks to a Gorenstein point and proves that a general element of |−K| around the exceptional divisor has at worst Du Val singularities. No arXiv version with this title exists in my searches; math/0110050 (event 7) has a different title. events.delivers: Per the search snippet only: for divisorial contractions to a Gorenstein point, a general element of |−K| near the exceptional divisor has at worst Du Val singularities.
events.remains: Divisorial contractions to non-Gorenstein points (see event 9 for a discrepancy-conditioned statement). The erratum's two classification gaps, which the erratum says are classification gaps.

checked_by.what_they_did: Restates a Kawakita divisorial-contraction theorem as proved (Thm 4.1 in the survey); no check of the proof reported

events.doubts: The erratum says the 2003 classification has two gaps. The erratum snippet also argues that a Du Val-type divisor can exist at cA1, cA2 and cD points, which suggests the gaps concern the classification rather than the Du Val claim. I did not read the erratum, so this is unverified. The record's date is the JAMS electronic date, not a preprint date; if math/0110050 is an earlier version of this work, its first public date is 4 October 2001 instead.
events.direction: Confirms the Du Val conclusion for the Gorenstein-point divisorial case, per the snippet.

events.what_happened: Kawakita, 'Three-fold divisorial contractions to singularities of higher indices', arXiv math/0306065 (v1 3 Jun 2003; 55 pages; a single version). The abstract (opened) says nothing about general elephants or Du Val singularities. It completes the study of divisorial contractions to a point, covers index n≥2 points with discrepancy conditions, and notes that the previous paper's erratum is attached. A search snippet of the body, which I did not open, says that when the discrepancy ratio is at most 1, the birational transform of a general elephant of X is a general elephant of Y with at worst Du Val singularities. Published in Duke Math. J. (2005) per a search snippet. AI check: abstract only; nothing names a system.
events.revisions: Single arXiv version; Duke 2005 per a snippet.
events.delivers: Per the body snippet only: for divisorial contractions to index n≥2 points with discrepancy ratio at most 1, the general elephant of X maps to a general elephant of Y with Du Val singularities. Not verified in the body.
events.remains: Discrepancy ratio greater than 1, which the abstract says has exceptions with arbitrarily large discrepancy and cD/2 type targets.
events.doubts: The Du Val claim rests on a snippet, and the abstract I read does not mention elephants. The same author's erratum concerns the same classification series.
events.direction: If the snippet is correct, confirms the Du Val conclusion in the index-n divisorial case with discrepancy ratio at most 1. Not verified.

events.what_happened: Alexeev, 'General elephants of Q-Fano 3-folds', Compositio Math. 91 (1994) 91–116 (MR 1273928). I opened only the Numdam bibliographic page, which has no abstract, so I could not read the paper. A search digest attributes to Alexeev the statement that if |−K_X| moves sufficiently, a Q-Fano threefold with only non-Du Val elephants is birational to one with a Du Val elephant; I could not verify this. AI check: nothing read names a system.
events.delivers: Unknown. The digest suggests a birational statement about Q-Fano threefolds with non-Du Val elephants; I did not check it against the paper.
events.doubts: Not read. Its content is unknown to me, so no direction is recorded.
events.direction: Unknown.

events.what_happened: Prokhorov, 'On the general elephant conjecture for Mori conic bundles', arXiv alg-geom/9608007 (v1 5 Aug 1996; 19 pages), Russ. Acad. Sci. Sb. Math. 188(11) (1997) 1665–1685. The paper states Conjecture I (for a Mori conic bundle f:(X,C)→(S,o), a general member of |−K_X| has only Du Val singularities) as a special case of Reid's conjecture. It assumes Conjecture I throughout Section 4 and derives a rough classification of Mori conic bundles (Thm 4.2) conditional on it. Read in the ar5iv rendering and the arXiv abstract. AI check: nothing read names a system.
events.delivers: Conditional: if Conjecture I holds, the base surface of a Mori conic bundle is smooth, A1, A3 (with a specific index-8 point), or a quotient of type A_(n−1). The paper does not prove Conjecture I.
events.remains: Conjecture I (Mori conic bundles over a smooth base), which this paper does not prove.

checked_by.who: Russian Academy of Sciences, Sbornik: Mathematics (journal)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 1997 (referee process not inspected)

events.doubts: Wikipedia's General elephant article lists this arXiv paper among the proved cases of the problem. The paper does not prove Conjecture I and its classification is conditional, so the article and the paper disagree (see disputes).
events.direction: Conditional on Conjecture I; no direction is given on the conjecture itself.

events.what_happened: Ducat, 'Divisorial extractions from singular curves in smooth 3-folds, I', arXiv 1403.7614 (v1 29 Mar 2014; a single version), Int. J. Math. 27 (2016), DOI 10.1142/S0129167X16500051. The abstract (opened) says: 'Assuming the general elephant conjecture, the general hypersurface section Γ⊂S⊂X is Du Val', and then constructs divisorial extractions from Γ, with terminal extractions excluded or classified for some surface types. AI check: abstract only; nothing names a system.

events.what_happened: Sano, 'Deforming elephants of Q-Fano threefolds', arXiv 1404.0909 (v1 3 Apr 2014; v2 11 Nov 2014; v3 22 Sep 2016; comment 'to appear in J. London Math. Soc.'; no journal reference found). Results (from the abstract page and the ar5iv rendering of the introduction): if a Q-Fano threefold X has an anticanonical divisor D with only isolated singularities, then (X,D) deforms to a Q-Fano with only quotient singularities and a Du Val elephant (a partial form of the Altınok–Brown–Reid deformation conjecture). It also gives Q-Fano threefolds with terminal quotient singularities whose anticanonical members are all non-Du Val (Example 4.4, per the introduction), and a quasi-smooth weighted hypersurface from Iano-Fletcher's list whose special equation has no Du Val elephant. Section 4 was truncated in my fetch. AI check: nothing read names a system.
events.delivers: (a) For Q-Fano threefolds whose anticanonical divisor has isolated singularities: deformation to a Du Val elephant, a non-Gorenstein deformation statement. It does not show that the general elephant of the given X is Du Val. (b) Examples of Q-Fano threefolds (terminal quotient singularities) whose anticanonical members are all non-Du Val (Example 4.4), and of a family with a special equation with no Du Val member. A separate Sano report, seen only as a snippet, gives an example with |−K_X| empty.
events.remains: Non-Gorenstein Q-Fano threefolds with no isolated-singularity anticanonical member. The Mori-contraction (local) form of the conjecture is outside this paper's stated scope.
events.directly_checkable: Example 4.4 and the weighted hypersurface examples are explicit equations in Sano's Section 4, which I could not read (fetch truncated); a checker would verify them directly.
events.doubts: Section 4, where the examples are worked out, was truncated in my fetch (100000 of 149925 characters). The explicit equation and weighted projective space for Example 4.4 are unverified. The introduction's wording ('may have empty anticanonical system or have only non-Du Val elephants') is from the fetched text, not checked against the printed paper. A separate source gives an explicit example S14 ⊂ P(2,2,3,7) with an elliptic singularity; I did not open it and do not record it as verified.
events.direction: Cuts against the literal bullet if the bullet is read over all threefolds with terminal singularities: in Example 4.4 every anticanonical member is non-Du Val, so the general member is non-Du Val. It does not touch the Mori-contraction (local) reading. Which reading applies is the judging pass's call.
events.object: Example 4.4: a Q-Fano threefold with only terminal quotient singularities whose anticanonical members are all non-Du Val (per the introduction; explicit equation not read). Also a quasi-smooth weighted hypersurface from Iano-Fletcher's list, with a special equation and no Du Val member of |−K_X|. Both are explicit examples, not existence proofs, as far as I can tell from the text.

events.what_happened: Jheng-Jie Chen, 'Normality of general elephants on 3-fold terminal flips', arXiv 1608.00364 (v1 1 Aug 2016). The v1 abstract (opened, condensed) claims that for a 3-fold terminal flip X⇢X⁺ the general elephant in |−K_{X⁺}| is normal, hence has at worst Du Val singularities, with a corollary excluding non-Gorenstein cE/2, cD/3 and cAx/4 singularities on the flipped curve. v2 (12 Aug 2016) is marked withdrawn; the comment says 'the main Theorem is a consequence of Theorem 2.2' of Kollár–Mori, Classification of three-dimensional flips. AI check: nothing read names a system.
events.revisions: v2 12 Aug 2016, withdrawn by the author.
events.delivers: Claimed in v1, then withdrawn: normality of the general elephant of a 3-fold terminal flip, hence Du Val. Nothing is delivered on the record.
events.remains: Nothing on the record. The author says the flip case follows from KM92 Theorem 2.2 (event 3).
events.doubts: Withdrawn by its author, who gives a reason (the result follows from KM92 Th 2.2). No other doubts recorded. The search found no engagement with the claim beyond the withdrawal.

withdrawn.what: v2 (12 Aug 2016) withdraws the paper, saying its main theorem is a consequence of Theorem 2.2 of Kollár–Mori, Classification of three-dimensional flips

events.direction: As claimed, confirms the Du Val conclusion in the flip case. Withdrawn, with the author treating the flip case as covered by KM92.

events.what_happened: A 2021 result by János Kollár, cited as 'Corollary 11' in an unidentified paper: if an elephant E through an isolated normal threefold singularity P has an isolated Du Val singularity at P, then P is a terminal singularity of X. Known only through the restatement as Theorem 5.1 in Kitagawa, arXiv 2412.14857 (v1 19 Dec 2024), which I saw as a search snippet; the arXiv abstract page I opened does not show it. I could not locate Kollár's paper, so the citation is unverified. AI check: nothing read names a system.
events.delivers: A terminality criterion: an isolated Du Val elephant forces terminal singularities at P. It concerns the singularity of X at P, not whether a general elephant is Du Val, so it does not settle the bullet.
events.doubts: Known only from a single restatement. The citing paper notes a characteristic-not-2 assumption for the Du Val definition.
events.direction: A converse-type criterion; not about the bullet's direction.

events.what_happened: Mori and Prokhorov, 'General elephants for threefold extremal contractions with one-dimensional fibers: exceptional case', arXiv 2002.10693 (v1 25 Feb 2020; v2 24 Mar 2020; v3 12 Jul 2020; v4 14 May 2021; v5 23 Sep 2024), Sbornik: Mathematics 212:3 (2021) 351–373, DOI 10.1070/SM9388. Theorem 1.3 (read in the v5 HTML, first 100000 of 136525 characters): for a germ (X,C) of a threefold with terminal singularities along a connected reduced complete curve C and a contraction f to (Z,o), if each irreducible component of C contains at most one point of index >2, then a general member D of |−K_X| is a normal surface with Du Val singularities. The paper restates the irreducible case (Thm 1.1, KM92 and MP09) and the Q-conic over singular base case (Thm 1.2, MP08b) as already known. AI check: the part read names no system; the acknowledgements are partly unread.
events.revisions: v2 24 Mar 2020; v3 12 Jul 2020; v4 14 May 2021; v5 23 Sep 2024, whose comment says 'one sentence in the introduction is corrected and Appendix B is added'. Footnote 1 of v5 says the original statement is not true as it stands because of the (IE∨) and (ID∨) cases, which move to the semistable extremal curve germs; only the (ID∨) case with P of type cAx/2 remains among the exceptional ones. Whether v1's Theorem 1.3 carried the same claim is not established by what I read. The journal version appeared in 2021, before v5. A 2025 remark by the same authors (event 17) comments on the 2021 paper.
events.delivers: Under the index hypothesis, the Du Val conclusion for a general member of |−K_X| for extremal curve germs with reducible central curve (Thm 1.3 as read in v5).
events.remains: Reducible central curves where some irreducible component contains two or more points of index greater than 2. The paper says more combinatorial restrictions will be treated in a subsequent paper; I found no such paper. Global (non-local) threefolds are outside this germ setting.

events.direction: Confirms the Du Val conclusion for reducible central curves under the index hypothesis, with a concession that an earlier version contained a false statement in some subcases.

disputes.summary: Wikipedia's General elephant article lists Prokhorov 1996 (arXiv alg-geom/9608007) among the proved cases. That paper assumes Conjecture I throughout and proves only a conditional classification of Mori conic bundles (event prokhorov-1996-conditional).

Kawakita's preprint erratum (December 2014) says the classification in his 2003 JAMS paper has two gaps, one identified by Yuki Yamamoto. Whether the gaps affect the Du Val general-element claim is not established from the erratum snippet (event kawakita-2002-jams-gorenstein-divisorial).

Mori and Prokhorov's arXiv v5 (23 September 2024) corrects a sentence in the introduction, saying the original statement was not true as it stands in the (IE∨) and (ID∨) cases. The 2025 Sbornik remark by the same authors is unread (events mori-prokhorov-2020-reducible and mori-prokhorov-remark-2025).

Mori's erratum to Kollár–Mori, Classification of three-dimensional flips (JAMS 20 (2007) 269–271), makes two corrections. It is unread, and I do not know whether either touches Theorem 2.2, which the irreducible-central-curve case rests on (event kollar-mori-1992-irreducible).
Chen's 2016 preprint on the general elephant of 3-fold terminal flips was withdrawn by its author, who says the main theorem follows from Kollár–Mori Theorem 2.2 (event chen-2016-flip-withdrawn).

summary: I ran 40 web searches and opened about 25 pages: the core arXiv papers (abstract, HTML or ar5iv), the Wikipedia article and the list entry, and Prokhorov's 2021 survey as HTML. The Wikipedia list entry reads 'do general elephants have at most Du Val singularities?' under Algebraic geometry, and the article's footer shows an edit in April 2026 that adds no recent results. No dated item after 26 January 2024 settles the threefold statement, and I found no counterexample to it in the local Mori-contraction setting. The window-era items are: (i) the 23 September 2024 revision (v5) of Mori and Prokhorov's 2020 partial result, which covers reducible central curves under an index-≤2 hypothesis and concedes that an earlier statement was false in two subcases; and (ii) a 2025 Sbornik remark by the same authors, whose content I could not read because Math-Net refused connections twice. Most of the record is pre-window. The irreducible-central-curve case rests on Kollár–Mori 1992 Theorem 2.2 and, for Q-conic bundles, on Mori–Prokhorov 2009; the Q-conic over singular base case is attributed to the 2007 Part II; Kawakita's divisorial-contraction cases are 2001 (cDV point), 2002/2003 (Gorenstein point) and 2003 (index n, discrepancy ratio at most 1, per a snippet); Mori conic bundles over a smooth base remain conditional (Prokhorov 1996, which Wikipedia lists as proved); and Sano's 2014 Q-Fano examples give anticanonical systems with only non-Du Val members. AI involvement: I searched for it explicitly (AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, Deep Think, Gemini, GPT, Claude, Epoch's FrontierMath Open Problems track, 2026 AI-math sweeps, and an acknowledgement search across the Fano-threefold literature). No source ties any AI system to this problem; the 2026 Gemini-assisted paper I found (R-equivalence on cubic surfaces) is a different problem. The AI check is limited to what I could read: the Mori–Prokhorov v5 acknowledgements are only partly read, and several sources (Kawakita, Sano's Section 4, the 2025 remark) were not read in full. Close calls: (a) whether Sano's Q-Fano examples count against the bullet depends on whether the bullet is read over all threefolds or over Mori contractions; (b) the Mori–Prokhorov Part III abstract says 'existence' of a Du Val member, not a general one, while the 2020 paper reads it as the general-member statement; (c) the Shokurov–Reid Gorenstein Fano result is described as 'an elephant' in one source and as the general member in another; (d) Wikipedia lists Prokhorov 1996 as proved although it is conditional.
competing_reading: Read the bullet as the literature does: Reid's conjecture for threefold contractions, a local statement. On that reading the record shows settled cases (irreducible central curve, KM92 Th 2.2 and MP09; Q-conic over a singular base, Part II as cited; reducible central curve under an index-≤2 hypothesis, Mori–Prokhorov 2020 with the 2024 correction; Kawakita's divisorial cases), conditional or open cases (Mori conic bundles over a smooth base; the general reducible case; flips beyond KM92), and nothing new in the window except the 2024 revision and the 2025 remark. Sano's Q-Fano examples fall outside that scope. The opposite reading takes the bullet literally, over all threefolds, with no restriction to contractions or Fano; then Sano's Example 4.4, whose anticanonical members are all non-Du Val, bears directly against the statement, whatever the local results say. A third reading uses the existence form of Mori–Prokhorov Part III, which would count as a weaker result than the general-member claim.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The text of the 2025 Mori–Prokhorov remark (Math-Net sm10194) and whether it corrects the 2021 theorem. (2) The v1 and v5 texts of arXiv 2002.10693: whether the corrected sentence changes Theorem 1.3's conclusion in the (IE∨) and (ID∨) cases. (3) Section 4 of Sano's arXiv 1404.0909: the explicit equation and weighted projective space for Example 4.4, and whether all its anticanonical members are non-Du Val. (4) The original Shokurov–Reid statement: whether it gives a general member or just some member, and its year. (5) Kollár's 2021 paper with Corollary 11, which I could not locate. (6) The body of Mori–Prokhorov Part III (0809.0489): whether the general member is proved there or only existence. (7) The intended scope of the Wikipedia bullet, which the article and the list do not state: the local Mori-contraction form or the Fano/Q-Fano form. The later pass should decide which before counting the Q-Fano examples.

judgement.why: Every substantive event predates the snapshot; all settle restricted settings (irreducible or index-restricted reducible central curves, Q-conic bundles over singular base, divisorial contractions of given types, Gorenstein Fano) and so are case, not whole. The Mori–Prokhorov 2020 paper keeps its 2020 date: the 2024 v5 corrects an introductory sentence and adds an appendix, which the record does not show to be new mathematics settling more of the problem. The only post-snapshot event, the 2025 Sbornik remark, has unknown content, so it is scored none — nothing in the record shows it settles or bounds anything. Sano's Q-Fano examples are scored a pre-snapshot case refutation under the literal, unrestricted reading of the statement (an explicit threefold whose general elephant is not Du Val); under the literature's Mori-contraction reading they would be a variant. Either way they predate the snapshot and do not make the problem resolved. Kollár's terminality criterion and Tanaka's positive-characteristic regularity result answer different questions (variant). No AI involvement in any event.
judgement.doubts: The 2025 Mori–Prokhorov remark is unread; if it extended Theorem 1.3, it could be a post-snapshot case. The statement's scope (local contraction form vs global/Q-Fano) is ambiguous; Sano's examples were scored as a case refutation on the literal wording, though under that reading the whole literal question might already be answered negatively before 2024.
